label: text
text: The "Daily Telegraph" Geneva correspondent says that a good deal of adverse comment has been aroused by the fact that despite China's inability to pay its annual subscription to the League or the coupons on the bonds, it entertained lavishly four hundred guests at one of the most fashionable hotels at a function that must have cost £1,000. It is recalled that public subscriptions had to be made for the starving people of China.

label: paragraph_title
text: LOANS COUPONS MET.

label: text
text: The “Times” City correspondent notes that the coupons due yesterday in two out of three Chinese loans were met, and an announcement with regard to the third is expected. He says it is to China's credit that despite political disorders, the service of foreign debt is maintained undisturbedly, except in a minor degree, and interest is at present being met on all secured Chinese loans issued in Britain with the exception noted.

label: text
text: London, June 3.—The assertion in Glasgow that Herr Stocker, a member of the Reichstag, did not attend the communist congress but was impersonated by a German resident, is confirmed at Cologne where authoritative Communist circles declare that neither Herr Stocker nor any other German Communist went to Glasgow in consequence of the British official embargo.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Sofia, June 3.—The Government has ordered the demobilisation of the ten thousand extra men which the Ambassadors' Conference permitted to be called to the Colours to deal with the Communist menace. The conference previously rejected the application for suspension of demobilisation. — Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: WHO OWNS THE POLE?

label: text
text: Official circles are perplexed at the report from Ottawa that Mr. Stewart, the Canadian Minister of the Interior told the Dominion House of Commons that Canada expects to claim any lands discovered north of Canada as far as the Pole. The forthcoming Macmillan expedition which will receive aid from the navy is intended to raise the Americann flag on any new land discovered which probably will be comparatively valueless except possibly as a future aviation base, but it is not thought that any serious American Canadian controversy will arise on the matter.

NEW SILK PLAN
A RAW MATERIAL
CONCESSION.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Methods for collecting the new silk taxes and payment of drawbacks on exported articles containing silk and artificial silk were discussed at a conference at the Treasury presided over by the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Mr. Winston Churchill, and attended by trade representatives and Government officials.

label: text
text: Mr. Churchill submitted a plan whereby duties will not be levied on raw material whether Home produced or imported which are intended to be utilised solely in the manufacture of export articles. Consequently no claim for a rebate will have to be established. The trade representatives will consider this scheme before communicating their views. Further discussions will be held on other points.

label: paragraph_title
text: RAILWAY SALVAGE.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: New York; June 3.

label: text
text: The Kuhn-Loeb Company announce a plan for the reorganisation of the Chicago Milwaukee and St. Paul Railroad, which provides for the exchange of over four hundred and sixty-four million dollars of securities and also the liquidation or funding of all short term debts and the assessment of $28 share preferred stock as $32 share common stock.

label: text
text: The plan also provides for a big reduction of the fixed interest bearing debt, the creation of a new share preference mortgage which will provide future capital expenditure and the creation of two additional mortgages.

label: text
text: The assessment plan will provide over seventy million dollars in cash, for which new five per cent. mortgage bonds will be issued. Allowing for the value of the bonds, a net assessment on stock of about nine dollars per share is indicated.

label: text
text: Ottawa, June 8.— Mr Mackenzie King announced in the House of Commons that the Government expected shortly to appoint a Canadian representative at Washington but difficulty was experienced in obtaining anyone willing to accept an account of the personal financial entity involved. The House of Commons there upon yield $60,000 to cover the salary and expenses of the post. Rober's American Service.

label: text
text: The rioters who fired on the Volunteers yesterday had taken up strategic positions, intending to fire on ratepayers motoring homeward in large numbers from the special meeting. The early termination of this upset their programme.

label: text
text: The strike situation in the international Settlement is slightly more tense. The fresh food markets and Chinese, shops are closed. The rioters are assaulting and otherwise terrorizing all Chinese remaining in the employment of foreigners; but the French Concession is so far unaffected.

label: text
text:
The students again held no public meeting yesterday, but the vernacular papers report various meetings in the colleges at which they made extravagant demands such as the withdrawal and punishment of the British Consultant General at Shanghai, the police who killed the students to be sentenced to death; an indemnity paid to the dead rioters' relatives; the British Government to be made to apologise to the Chinese people, in addition to demands for the return of concessions, etc.
It understood that the National University, which usually leads student agitators has decided to strike from today as a protest, and is calling all students to gather there to day for a demonstration against “British Imperialism,” also urging that all economic relations be severed with Great Britain and Japan, and that (Chinese) deposits be withdrawn from (British and Japanese) banks, the banknotes of the two countries not to be accepted and no provisions to be sold to their nationals, Chinese employees to be induced to leave British and Japanese employers and students to leave their schools.

label: paragraph_title
text: Reaching A Settlement

label: text
text: In connection with the efforts of the Chinese merchants to devise some form of compromise, which will end the present disorders and save the faces of the Municipal Council and students, the “North-China Daily News,” editorially believes that the idea is that the students should withdraw the pickets and declare peace. The matter can be referred to Peking for adjustment. The paper says, however, that any interference by the Waichiaopu should be directed towards the students after the fashion of the order recently issued in Peking, ordering the students back to their classrooms.

label: text
text: “We appreciate the efforts of the Chinese merchants to restore order, but as these efforts are being directed at present, we tell them frankly that they are wasting their time. There is only one way in which peace can be brought back; that is by the unconditional surrender of the students and other agitators”

label: paragraph_title
text: Peking To Investigate.

label: text
text: The Government has appointed Mr. Tsai Ting-ken and Mr. Tseng Tsung-Chien (Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs) as High Commissioner to investigate the Shanghai affair. They are expected to leave for there tomorrow.

label: text
text: The Waichiaopu sent a Note this afternoon to the Italian Minister in his capacity as Senior Minister of the interested Powers, relative to the Shanghai situation. The Note protests against the shooting of the students and requests him to bring the Note to the knowledge of the interested Powers.

label: text
text: The Foreign Office's protest reserves "the right to formulate claims which may result from this deplorable incident, for which the authorities of the International Concession are entirely responsible." The Note requests the Ministers to give "urgent necessary instruction to the Consular Authorities in Shanghai to set at liberty those arrested."

At dawn the air began to throb with a tempest of drums as the southern chiefs assembled for review by the Prince. It was to just such a menacing clangour that 30 years ago the British garrisons used to listen as the invading Ashanti army approached the coast.
All the splendour of the palaver at Kumasi, the Ashanti capital, was reproduced, with the strange additions of devil-dancers with crocodile-head masks. Not only the richness of their fantastic accoutrements but also the personal dignity of these inky dignitaries make average British mayors and aldermen seem by comparison awkward; tawdry, and uncouth.
